description: The HIT-UAV research team publishes 2,898 infrared images for detecting people and vehicles from unmanned aircraft. Images cover schools, parking areas, roads and playgrounds, with flight altitudes of 60–130 metres and viewing angles of 30–90 degrees. Standard and oriented bounding-box annotations are supplied in XML and JSON. The repository also contains Python conversion and visualisation tools. Access is free; the archived Zenodo release states CC0, while the current GitHub repository states CC BY 4.0. The observations can test detection components for emergency-response or traffic simulations, alongside model-sumo. A caveat is that scene coverage is selective, and infrared recognition accuracy does not directly establish operational search performance. The Chinese tool documentation marks its AP evaluator as unfinished and unsuitable for oriented boxes. No images or code were downloaded or run.
